newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Stop "persecuting" dissident, democrats tell China.
newsitem.headline: Stop "persecuting" dissident, democrats tell China.

text.p: Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement petitioned Beijing on Friday to stop "persecuting" imprisoned top dissident Wei Jingsheng and set him free.

About 20 members from the Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movement in China, led by chairman Szeto Wah, mounted a protest outside China's Hong Kong mission and left a letter accusing Beijing of having Wei beaten up in jail.
Wei is serving a 14-year jail term for subversion.
The protesters said a softer Western stance towards China's human rights record had aggravated the plight of Wei and other jailed dissidents.

"There is a policy by the Communist Party that it does not allow the beating up of prominent dissidents...so the beating of Wei Jingsheng is totally political persecution," said activist Lau Shan-ching, speaking from his own experience.
Lau is a Hong Kong activist who was jailed in China for 10 years for urging more democracy in 1979.

"The Alliance urges the people of Hong Kong not to forget those who are in jail during the handover," said Szeto, reading out a petition letter that the protesters handed in at the Xinhua news agency branch, China's official mission.
He urged people not to forget China's human rights situation and called on China to stop persecuting dissenters.
"China should immediately release Wei Jingsheng and all other dissidents," he said.

Prison authorities have recently accused Wei, the father of China's struggling democracy movement, of brawling with another inmate and have imposed new punishments, a family member who visited him in mid-June said.
Electricity to Wei's cell has been cut off and he has been banned from shopping at the prison canteen, said the relative, who expressed concern about Wei's health.

Xinhua officials did not come out to receive the letter, so the group left it on the doorstep of the Xinhua building in Happy Valley, across the street from Hong Kong's Jockey Club, a bastion of colonial tradition.
Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, and the alliance, viewed as subversive by Beijing fears for its future.
China has persuaded future Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa to bring in curbs on political liberties including a ban on demonstrations that threaten "national security".
